## Final hypothesis (data-grounded)

**No SES level in this sample shows a Black completion-rate advantage; the Black–other BA gap is negative at every socioeconomic level. The disadvantage is most pronounced in the lower-middle SES band (2nd SES quintile, SES ≈ −0.59 to −0.24, where Black students complete a BA at 0.88% vs 3.62% for others, a −2.74 pp gap), while at the highest SES levels (top quintile, SES > 0.54) the gap essentially disappears — 3.45% vs 3.54% (−0.10 pp, 95% CI −2.47 to +2.78, statistically indistinguishable).** In other words, socioeconomic advantage at the top of the SES distribution is associated with parity in BA completion for Black students, whereas the mid-low SES range is where their completion rates fall furthest behind non-Black peers. Formally: the SES×Black logistic interaction is positive and significant (coef 0.627, SE 0.250, p = 0.012), i.e., the Black completion penalty shrinks monotonically with SES.

## Bin-level table (PRIMARY: 5 equal-frequency SES bins)

| Bin | SES range | n Black | Black BA% (95% CI) | n Other | Other BA% (95% CI) | Gap pp (95% CI) | Ratio B/O |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (lowest) | −2.45 to −0.59 | 525 | 0.19 (0.03–1.07) | 1230 | 0.89 (0.50–1.59) | −0.70 (−1.38, −0.06) | 0.21 |
| 2 | −0.59 to −0.24 | 567 | 0.88 (0.38–2.05) | 1187 | 3.62 (2.70–4.84) | **−2.74 (−4.00, −1.46)** | 0.24 |
| 3 | −0.24 to +0.11 | 491 | 2.24 (1.26–3.97) | 1267 | 3.47 (2.60–4.63) | −1.23 (−2.93, +0.54) | 0.65 |
| 4 | +0.11 to +0.54 | 327 | 1.22 (0.48–3.10) | 1424 | 3.86 (2.98–4.99) | **−2.64 (−4.13, −0.97)** | 0.32 |
| 5 (highest) | +0.54 to +2.72 | 203 | 3.45 (1.68–6.95) | 1552 | 3.54 (2.73–4.58) | **−0.10 (−2.47, +2.78)** | 0.97 |

Ranking by |gap| (most pronounced first): **bin 2 > bin 4 > bin 3 > bin 1 > bin 5** (least pronounced/most near-parity: top quintile).

## Robustness & comparator choices that affect the ranking

- **Quartiles:** largest gap in Q2 (−0.48 ≤ SES < −0.08): −2.56 pp; top quartile near parity (−0.65 pp, CI −2.74 to +1.72). Ranking: Q2 > Q3 > Q1 > Q4.
- **Terciles:** largest gap shifts to the lowest tercile (−1.74 pp) because the mid-low bins merge; top tercile −1.51 pp (CI includes 0). Coarser binning smooths the mid-bin spike, but "top SES bin ≈ parity" holds in every scheme.
- **Black vs White only (quintiles):** largest gaps in bins 2 and 4 (−3.18 and −2.92 pp); vs Hispanic: gaps much smaller (max −0.87 pp), and bin 3 even shows a small positive gap (+0.41 pp Black > Hispanic) — the only "advantage-like" signal, driven by Hispanic rates being uniformly low. Pooled non-Black and White comparators agree on the main pattern; Hispanic comparisons do not.
- **Sex-stratified (quintiles):** pattern holds for both sexes; the top bin is the only place a positive gap appears at all (Male bin 5: +0.19 pp; Female bin 5: −0.42 pp) — negligible and within noise.
- **Caveat on bin 1 (lowest SES):** the absolute gap looks small (−0.70 pp) only because completion is near-floor for everyone; the relative ratio (0.21) is actually the second-worst, so the low-SES disadvantage is real but floors compress the pp metric.

## Diagnostics / limitations
- 2,000-replicate bootstrap CIs for gaps; Wilson CIs for rates. Total BAs = 236, so bin estimates are noisy (e.g., 1 BA among 525 Black students in bin 1); several bin CIs overlap.
- No survey weights, cohort, or follow-up-age variables available; results are descriptive associations, not causal.
- SES bins are equal-frequency on a continuous standardized index (range −2.45 to 2.72); zero missingness anywhere in the 8,773-row dataset.

payload.hypothesis: No SES level shows a Black completion-rate advantage; the Black-vs-other BA gap is negative at every level. The disadvantage is most pronounced in the lower-middle SES band (2nd quintile, SES −0.59 to −0.24: 0.88% vs 3.62%, −2.74 pp; similarly the 4th quintile −2.64 pp), and essentially disappears at the highest SES levels (top quintile, SES > 0.54: 3.45% vs 3.54%, −0.10 pp, CI −2.47 to +2.78). The SES×Black logistic interaction is positive and significant (+0.627, p=0.012), i.e., the Black completion penalty shrinks with SES, reaching near-parity at the top of the SES distribution.
payload.workflow: Loaded nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 rows, zero missingness). Binned continuous SES into equal-frequency quintiles (primary), quartiles and terciles (robustness). Within each bin compared BA completion rates of Black vs non-Black (pooled; secondary Black-vs-White and Black-vs-Hispanic), reporting absolute pp gaps with 2,000-replicate bootstrap CIs, Wilson CIs for rates, and Black/other ratios. Sex-stratified replication and logistic GLM (BA ~ SES + Black + SES×Black) as continuous checks. Ranking by |gap|: quintile bins 2 and 4 most pronounced, top bin near-parity; pattern robust across bin counts and sexes, with the Hispanic-only comparator the main divergence.
